analysis.title: Americas Utilities: Power - Early views on key state election results for power/utilities; potential risk to TX exposed stocks including NRG/VST
key_insights: Goldman Sachs focuses on four state elections (TX, GA, OH, CA) for their effect on data center development, the pace of power demand, pricing, utility investment and wildfire liability reform.

Democratic wins could raise near-term uncertainty around data center development, especially in Texas and Georgia. GS still sees both as important long-term load growth markets, consistent with its Macro team's post-election views.

Texas: Gina Hinojosa (D) beat Governor Greg Abbott (R). She has called for a data center moratorium until the legislature adds protections in 2027. GS sees this as a risk to the timing of development, not the long-term opportunity.

Texas exposure: GS sees potential risk to the timing of the load growth inflection, which could affect ERCOT power prices and regulated utility capex. The next datapoint is the data center audit study due by December 10.

Georgia: Democrats flipped the Public Service Commission to a majority (Peter Hubbard re-elected, Shelia Edwards won her district), and Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) won the governorship over Rick Jackson (R). Edwards has previously supported a data center moratorium in Georgia.
Georgia: GS expects more uncertainty for continued large-load investment. SO is most exposed, with 56% of its rate base in the state and a 75 GW+ prospective large load pipeline.

Ohio: Amy Acton (D) beat Vivek Ramaswamy (R). GS expects about 8 GW of data centers online by 2030 and sees results as slightly increasing uncertainty, with potentially stricter requirements and more community focus.

California: Xavier Becerra (D) won the governorship over Steve Hilton (R). Governor Newsom could still call a special legislative session on wildfire liability reform before November 15th, otherwise the decision passes to the new administration.
California: Becerra has said more work is needed on wildfire policy. GS sees reform as still a priority, with timing and scope unclear. A special session could be positive for PCG, SRE and EIX.
Exhibit 1 shows the elections flipped party control in TX, GA and OH, with CA staying Democratic.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic wins in TX, GA and OH add near-term uncertainty to data center development. GS keeps a long-term constructive view on load growth in these markets.

risk_factors: Texas moratorium on data center interconnection until 2027 legislative protections could delay load growth and ERCOT price upside.
Georgia PSC majority change could slow large load investment and affect SO's 75 GW+ pipeline.
Ohio data center requirements could tighten and community focus could rise.
California wildfire liability reform could slip to the new administration if no special session is called.
Stock-level risks: VST and NRG face PJM capacity auction uncertainty and lower power prices, FE faces its Ohio rate case, and AEP faces adverse data center tariff decisions in Texas or Ohio.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 lists the gubernatorial race ratings and outcomes: Texas (Likely/Lean Republican, Democratic win), Georgia (Toss-up, Democratic win), Ohio (Lean Democratic, Democratic win), California (Solid/Safe Democratic, Democratic win).
geopolitical: Democrats won the gubernatorial races in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and California on the November 2026 state election day.
Georgia's Public Service Commission flipped to a Democratic majority.
Governor Newsom could call a special legislative session on wildfire liability reform before November 15th.
The report notes federal election results could also have implications but does not cover them.

tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa has called for a data center moratorium until the legislature adds protections in 2027, which could delay the load growth inflection, ERCOT power prices and regulated utility capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The data center audit study due by December 10 is the next datapoint GS watches.

tension_points.what_invalidates: No special session called by November 15th.
